subject: CopperRidge private cluster: sudden throughput collapse — exec escalation
messages:
From: ops@copperridge.health
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Production: 504s & throughput drop on CopperRidge private cluster

Marcus —

We started seeing a spike of 504s and a sharp drop in QPS on our on-prem cluster around 08:50 PT. Traffic looks normal from the app side; inference latency P95 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.1s and many requests are returning 504. We’ve attached a short snippet of logs from the API gateway and a flamegraph for node-3. Can you confirm this is on Redwood’s side? This is impacting clinical triage workflows.

Urgent — please advise on rollback or mitigation steps.

— Ali
Ali Aslan
CTO, CopperRidge Health
ali@copperridge.health
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: ops@copperridge.health, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: 504s & throughput drop on CopperRidge private cluster

Thanks Ali — I’m escalating immediately. Laura (AM) and Jonas (SRE) are looping in. Initial ask: can you confirm the last deploy window and any config changes on your orchestration side in the last 2 hours? We will collect server-side metrics, kernel traces, and check our model variant routing.

Short-term: we will enable a conservative fallback policy to the pre-quantized model variant and reduce batch windows for the affected pool (canary first). If we need a faster mitigation we’ll coordinate a forced rollback.

I’ve attached the logs you sent and will share our runbook proposal in the next update. ETA for first triage update: 30 minutes.

— Marcus Lin
Senior Mgr, Customer Success 
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: 504s & throughput drop on CopperRidge private cluster

Triage notes (quick):
- Checked node telemetry for their private cluster (agent traces) — node-3 shows CPU steal and kernel preemption spikes coincident with increased latency.
- Inference runtime: a recent config flip to 4-bit quantized kernels (applied 08:40 PT) matches timeframe.
- KV cache hit rates are lower on larger sequence inputs after quantization; this increases per-request token work.
- We see increased RPC time between orchestrator -> runtime for pooled requests (possible backpressure).

Immediate plan:
1) Start canary rollback of model variant on one pool (node-1) to previous FP16 runtime (reduce amplification).
2) Temporarily tighten batching to max_batch=8 and max_wait_ms=8 for affected pools.
3) If CPU steal persists, propose adding one utility GPU to the pool (burst capacity) or shifting low-priority batch jobs off those machines.

I’ll run the canary now and post logs. If the canary improves P95 we can do a staged rollback.

— Jonas Weber
SRE, Platform Reliability
From: Ali Aslan <ali@copperridge.health>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: 504s & throughput drop on CopperRidge private cluster

Thanks — confirmed: our deployment pipeline pushed a config bundle at 08:38 PT that enabled the new quantization profile (says: q4_k_v2). No other orchestration changes. We’ve paused any further deployments.

Please prioritize rollback if quantization is the likely cause. This is directly impacting ER workflows. We need an ETA and a communication to our ops team for expected recovery window.

— Ali
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Ali Aslan <ali@copperridge.health>
Date: 2027-04-22T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: 504s & throughput drop on CopperRidge private cluster

Update for execs & AM plan:
- Canary rollback to FP16 on pool-a (nodes 1–2) complete at 11:45 PT. Observed P95 drop from ~2.1s -> 140ms on canary traffic within 3 minutes. Node-3 still elevated and showing kernel preemption.
- Action requested from CopperRidge: allow temporary burst capacity (add one GPU to node-3 or permit redistribution). If they cannot, we need to coordinate a machine reboot with maintenance window.
- Proposed runbook (attached runbook-proposed-tuning-v1.pdf): kernel scheduling flags, kv-cache pre-warm prior to rollout, and stricter per-pool batching caps.

Ask to leadership: we should authorize emergency burst credit for CopperRidge (up to 12 hours) and a priority kernel/compile pass to produce a quantization-aware kernel selection for q4_k_v2. Karthik — can you advise on kernel compile ETA and whether we should push a hotpatch?

— Marcus
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Ali Aslan <ali@copperridge.health>
Date: 2027-04-22T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: 504s & throughput drop on CopperRidge private cluster

Karthik here — short note on feasibility and next steps:
- Kernel/compile: we can prioritize a quantization-aware kernel pass for q4_k_v2. Estimated time-to-build+validation for a hotpatch: ~18–24 hours (accelerated). We will need dedicated CI cycle and a quick canary validation window.
- Immediate remediation: approve temporary burst capacity (one GPU) and allow us to roll back quantized variant from remaining nodes. That buys us time to validate the hotpatch without causing production impact.
- Commercial/ops: Marcus — I support emergency burst credits for up to 12 hours. Laura — please prepare a short customer-facing note indicating expected recovery and that we will follow with a kernel fix timeline.

Next milestones:
1) Customer confirmation on burst capacity (decision within 30 minutes).
2) If approved, we add capacity and complete rollback by 17:30 PT.
3) Begin 18–24 hour hotpatch work and schedule validation.

— Karthik Iyer
VP, Serving Runtime Engineering
